misconception_description: Student believes that while loops execute their body only once if the condition is true.

solutions.generated_code:
program CariTerkecil
kamus
  n, i, x, terkecil : integer
algoritma
  input(n)
  input(x)
  terkecil <- x
  i <- 2
  while i <= n do
    input(x)
    if x < terkecil then
      terkecil <- x
    endif
  endwhile
  output(terkecil)
endprogram

metadata.modification_notes: The student rewrote the for loop as a while loop but failed to increment the counter variable `i`. Since the student believes while loops execute their body only once (like an if statement would), they think the loop will check list1[1] once, update min_val if needed, and then exit. From their perspective, there's no need to increment `i` because they expect the while loop to run just once and stop. In reality, this creates an infinite loop because `i` remains 1 forever, and the condition `i < len(list1)` stays true indefinitely (assuming the list has more than one element). The student genuinely believes this will correctly check one additional element beyond the first and return the minimum value.
